intro: Geneva rewards visitors with a compact old town, a sparkling lakefront and easy access to the Alps. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Trams and buses run by TPG cover most of the city; buy tickets at stop machines before boarding.
A one-hour ticket costs about CHF 3; a day pass about CHF 8.
Hotels and hostels often give a free Unireso transport card at check-in.
Taxis are metered and pricey; ride apps like Uber operate in Geneva.
The city is fairly flat and good for bikes; Genèveroule lends bikes free in summer.
Yellow 'mouette' boats cross the lake and are covered by TPG tickets.

jetdeau.name: Jet d'Eau
jetdeau.hours: Runs daily; often daytime into evening in season. Check on the day.
jetdeau.tip: Walk out to the pier at the jetty base for the closest view and a light spray.

unog.name: United Nations Office at Geneva
unog.price_text: Guided tour fee varies; check on the day
unog.hours: Weekday guided tours; book ahead. Check on the day.
unog.tip: Bring your passport for the security check and book a tour slot online in advance.

stpierre.name: St. Pierre Cathedral
stpierre.price_text: Church free; tower climb small fee, check on the day
stpierre.hours: Open daily; shorter hours on Sunday. Check on the day.

lakegenevatour.name: Lake Geneva Tour
lakegenevatour.price_text: Boat cruises roughly CHF 20–40 for short trips; check on the day
lakegenevatour.hours: Departures through the day; seasonal timetable
lakegenevatour.tip: A short one-hour cruise from the Mont-Blanc pier is enough for first-timers.

telepherique.name: Téléphérique du Salève
telepherique.price_text: Return ticket roughly CHF 15–20; check on the day
telepherique.hours: Closed Mondays in some seasons; check on the day
telepherique.tip: It crosses into France, so bring ID. The ridge walk gives wide views of the city and lake.

unige.name: University of Geneva
unige.tip: The Bastions park next door is a calm green stop with the Reformation Wall.

plainpalais_market.name: Plainpalais Flea Market
plainpalais_market.hours: Some mornings, often Wednesday and Saturday; check on the day
plainpalais_market.tip: Come early for the best stalls and bring small cash.

carouge_walk.name: Carouge Neighbourhood Walk
carouge_walk.hours: Always open; shops closed on Sunday
carouge_walk.tip: Wander the small streets and squares for cafes and independent shops.

oldtown_walk.name: Old Town Walk
oldtown_walk.tip: Start at Place du Bourg-de-Four and climb to the cathedral.

bastions.name: Parc des Bastions
bastions.tip: See the giant chess boards and the Reformation Wall at the far end.

bains_des_paquis.name: Bains des Pâquis
bains_des_paquis.price_text: Small entry fee for swimming; check on the day
bains_des_paquis.tip: Swim in the lake and grab a simple meal at the pier cafe.

broken_chair.name: Broken Chair Monument
broken_chair.tip: A quick photo stop on the way to the UN district.

english_garden.name: Jardin Anglais
english_garden.tip: See the flower clock and the lakeside promenade here.

patek.name: Patek Philippe Museum
patek.price_text: Entry fee roughly CHF 10–15; check on the day
patek.hours: Closed Monday; check on the day
patek.tip: A deep dive into watchmaking history; allow a couple of hours.

red_cross.name: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum
red_cross.price_text: Entry fee roughly CHF 15; check on the day
red_cross.hours: Closed Monday; check on the day
red_cross.tip: Pair it with the UN district nearby for a full half-day.

rues_basses.name: Rues Basses Shopping Walk
rues_basses.tip: Walk the main shopping streets from the station down to the lake.

mont_saleve_view.name: Salève Ridge Viewpoint
mont_saleve_view.tip: Walk a short way along the ridge for the widest lake view.

plaine_de_plainpalais.name: Plaine de Plainpalais
plaine_de_plainpalais.tip: A big open square used for markets and fairs; check what is on.

mamco.name: MAMCO Contemporary Art Museum
mamco.price_text: Entry fee roughly CHF 10–15; check on the day
mamco.hours: Closed Monday; check on the day
mamco.tip: A good indoor stop near Plainpalais on a wet day.

eauxvives_promenade.name: Eaux-Vives Lakeside Promenade
eauxvives_promenade.tip: Walk east along the lake for quiet views and small beaches.

stays.why: Steps from the cathedral, museums and the lake; quiet at night but hilly cobbled lanes.
Central and lively, close to the station and the lake; many budget hotels and cheap eats.
Leafy and local, near the lake beaches and parks; good for families and longer stays.
Student and arts quarter with a flea market; tram links to both banks, good value.

food: Try fondue or raclette in the Old Town; portions are big, so share one between two.
Lake fish (perch fillets, 'filets de perche') is a local favourite; ask for the day's catch.
Cheap eats: Pâquis has kebab shops, falafel and Asian cafeterias, roughly CHF 10–20 a meal.
Pick up bread, cheese and fruit at a market or supermarket for a picnic by the lake; it saves a lot.
Restaurant prices are high. Lunch menus ('menu du jour') cost less than dinner; book popular places ahead.
more_time: Take a boat trip on Lake Geneva (Les Mouettes or CGN cruises) to see the city and the Alps from the water.
Swap a city afternoon for a day trip to Montreux or Lausanne by train; check times and prices on the day.
Cross into France for a cheaper lunch in Annemasse or a walk along the lake shore; bring your passport.
